There is a real difference. `structuredClone` keeps `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, `undefined` and circular references, while the JSON round trip turns dates into strings, drops `undefined` and functions, and throws on cycles; `structuredClone` throws on functions and DOM nodes. So prefer `structuredClone`, and keep the JSON trick only when you want a JSON-safe copy on purpose.
Action: none needed; tell me if you want me to swap any existing JSON-trick copies.

The common thread: every error is TS1484, a name that is only a type being imported as a regular value, which `verbatimModuleSyntax` forbids because it keeps imports exactly as written. The fix is `import type { X }` or `import { type X }` for each one, and it's mechanical; a lint autofix like a use-import-type rule can do most of it.
Action: run typecheck to get the full list of sites, apply the type-only import fixes, and re-run typecheck until clean.

With htmx the token isn't sent automatically: a `hx-post` request only carries the CSRF token if it's in the form that gets posted or in a header. Most likely the partial's form no longer contains `{% csrf_token %}`, or you render the partial without the request so the token is empty. Fixes: put `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form, or set `hx-headers='{"X-CSRFToken": "{{ csrf_token }}"}'` on the body in the base template.
Action: ask you to paste the partial and the view that renders it, so I can tell which of those it is.
